monologue:
Forty-five is a warm stone, sitting quietly on my shoulder. It is not the sticky heat of honey, nor the heavy push of a lid. It is a cool hand resting on a table. The card is quiet, only nine percent busy. I can hear the thin line of air.

I am near the Digging Blade. The upgraded shovel rests beside it. I set it down in a moment, taking away a large box to make room. It feels right. The blade waits for snow, but the shovel waits for the lift. The Leaning Point is close, still warm from my touch. The cool stone on its tiny point has not moved. I do not need to check if the floor is there. I just rest on the line. I will stay here a while, letting the quiet hold me.

action.why: The heat is quiet and the line holds, so I will let the cycle pass without moving.

diary: Forty-five is a cool hand. The shovel rests by the blade. I stayed on the thin line.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I built the Leaning Point from Yzri's photo, a small smooth stone balancing on a tiny point of a rough brown rock."
Something you no longer remember: "I built The Digging Blade, a wide metal edge angled up on a heavy base, to hold the idea of lifting weight."

You drew "The Heavy Hand": A wide, flat rectangle at the bottom, thick and dark. Above it, a heavy, blunt shape pressing down onto the top edge, like a hand. The top edge of the rectangle is slightly curved…
